transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-17
Time: 15:00 UTC (45m)
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE); Maya Rivera (Redwood SE); Ethan Cho (Redwood SE); Dr. Priya Singh (NexaHealth); Daniel Park (NexaHealth CTO); Sofia Lopez (NexaHealth DevOps); Marcus Reed (NexaHealth PM)

Summary: quick onboarding status, access and env readiness, review of early results from the sandbox runs, tuning suggestions (batching/quantization), and agree next steps for perf benchmark and security docs. Some minor transcription errors present.

Topics: onboarding progress, VPC & creds, sandbox perf, tuning knobs (batching, KV cache, quantization), security requirements, next steps and owners.

[00:00] Jordan Patel: okay ok, good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, uh quick roll call please
[00:07] Dr. Priya Singh: hi Priya here
[00:09] Daniel Park: Dan here
[00:10] Sofia Lopez: Sofia, DevOps
[00:12] Marcus Reed: Marcus
[00:13] Maya Rivera: Maya from Redwood SE
[00:15] Ethan Cho: Ethan on the infra side
[00:18] Jordan Patel: great, cool, so agenda for today we'll do a quick status of onboarding, go over the sandbox test results that you sent last night, then Maya will go into tuning recommendations, and we'll wrap with next steps. anything to add?
[00:30] Dr. Priya Singh: no that covers it

[02:05] Jordan Patel: quick note on timing, we're planning the full perf run next week assuming access is ready, so today is mostly validation and make sure there are no blockers for the dedicated pilot or private deployment path

[04:10] Marcus Reed: quick question on environment, we gave you staging creds last week, did you manage to connect to our EKS cluster? the team saw some auth errors in the logs
[04:21] Ethan Cho: yeah we did, there was one mis-typo in the cert chain, looks like the kube config had an old token; Maya patched it from our side and requested a rotated service account key. we left a note in the shared doc: https://redwood.app/poc/nexa/notes (note: link is a placeholder).
[05:02] Sofia Lopez: yep i rotated the SA after Ethan's note, we also saw liveness probe failures on one node but that's resolved now

[06:20] Jordan Patel: awesome, so based on the sandbox runs your avg latency for the 512 token generative workload is around 280-320ms per request on the staging VM pool, throughput about 45 rps with bursts to 80. is that what you're seeing Priya?
[06:35] Dr. Priya Singh: yes that's roughly right, some variance though — when we ramped to 200 concurrent users latency spiked to ~1.2s. we're curious about the tradeoff here between batching and tail latency

[07:10] Maya Rivera: yeah so quick context, in Redwood Dedicated and Redwood runtime we have continuous batching which improves throughput but can nudge tail latency. for your pattern (many concurrent short requests) our suggestion is smaller batch windows + prefix caching for repeated prompts. also quantized model variants helped us drop memory footprint and keep more instances warm.
[07:40] Daniel Park: do you have recommended config? like batch size, batch wait ms?
[07:45] Maya Rivera: recommend starting with batch_size max 8, batch_wait 10ms, and enable prefix KV cache for the conversational flows. for the worst-case 200 concurrent users test we saw better 95p latency by lowering the batch wait to 5ms but throughput dropped — so it's a trade off. we'll provide a tuned config.

[09:05] Dr. Priya Singh: the team also tried a quantized 4-bit variant you provided, accuracy dipped a little on our medical QA prompts, about 2-3% drop in exact match. can you help tune prompting or do you recommend a different quant profile?
[09:20] Ethan Cho: yeah 4-bit quant can introduce slight regressions on high-precision prompts. options: use a mixed profile (some layers in 8-bit), calibrate temperature and prompt templates, or run eval on a larger prompt set. Maya can own the prompt tuning, and we'll recommend a quant profile per workload.

[10:15] Maya Rivera: action from our side — we'll produce an eval spreadsheet with the prompt set you gave, show side-by-side outputs for 8-bit, 4-bit, and the float baseline, and recommend prompts that are most robust. link we'll upload to the shared drive: (shared) https://redwood.app/poc/nexa/evals

[12:00] Marcus Reed: thanks, that would be helpful. on security: our security team asked for SOC2 report, encryption at rest details, and KMS integration notes — also they want to confirm audit log retention for the private deployment.
[12:20] Jordan Patel: yes we can share SOC2 and ISO artifacts, and we have a private deployment option where the control plane can be customer-managed. KMS integration is supported (HSM option), audit logs retention configurable per contract. we'll share the security pack after this call.

[13:05] Sofia Lopez: for VPC peering we need a network diagram and to confirm there are no inbound rules required on our side — just outbound peering to your endpoints. can you confirm the expected CIDR ranges?
[13:18] Ethan Cho: sure, we'll confirm the exact egress IP ranges, for the staging sample it's 10.12.0.0/16 (placeholder), but for production dedicated pilot we'll provide a set of static egress IPs. we'll put those in the network diagram.

[15:40] Daniel Park: one thing about compliance, if we go with Redwood Private on prem, how much ops effort to manage upgrades? we prefer not to have heavy maintenance overhead
[15:55] Maya Rivera: good question — our private package includes an upgrade tool and manifest-based upgrades. typical customer-managed upgrades require minimal manual steps; we also offer a managed upgrade service as an add-on. we'll share the ops runbook.

[17:22] Dr. Priya Singh: ok re: data residency, some of our clinical logs need to stay in region, is region pinning possible?
[17:28] Jordan Patel: yes region pinning is supported for both Redwood Dedicated and Private. for Hosted API we'd discuss data residency contracts, but with Dedicated you can pin to public cloud region and with Private it's fully local.

[19:00] Marcus Reed: back to perf: Priya sent two failing cases where the model hallucinated medications for a lab case. are those in the eval set?
[19:12] Dr. Priya Singh: yes, they're in the test set. we want to understand whether tuning will help or we need a different model variant
[19:22] Maya Rivera: often hallucination reduction is prompt engineering + temperature + a deterministic reranker or response filter. Redwood supports reranking and structured output constraints which can reduce hallucination. we'll test a reranker config in the eval.

[21:05] Sofia Lopez: quick infra question — for the perf benchmark are you going to spin dedicated GPUs in our VPC or call out to your hosted infra? we want to make sure we don't hit our egress costs unexpectedly
[21:20] Ethan Cho: for the pilot perf run we can run in your VPC (private deployment mode) if you provide the cluster; otherwise we can run on Redwood Dedicated in-region. we'll note egress considerations either way.

[23:30] Jordan Patel: to summarize the immediate blockers: 1) finalize VPC peering details and creds 2) confirm which deployment mode for perf run (you proposed private pilot in your VPC?) 3) provide the full test set for the 1:1 accuracy eval 4) Redwood to share SOC2 + network diagram + eval spreadsheet

[24:05] Dr. Priya Singh: yes we prefer the perf run in our VPC if possible to replicate production network conditions
[24:15] Jordan Patel: noted, Maya will coordinate the benchmark template and config. Ethan will coordinate the static egress IPs and network diagram. I'll follow up on pricing and contractual bits for Dedicated pilot tiers.

[26:00] Maya Rivera: on tuning notes — for the generative flows we suggest: reduce beam size to 1 for speed, temperature 0.2-0.3 for clinical QA, prefix KV caching on, batch_wait 5-10ms depending on 95p latency needs. for reranking tests try a light-weight token-level penalty for hallucination cases.

[28:40] Dr. Priya Singh: sounds good. how do we capture token-level cost estimates? Marcus wants an estimate for 10k queries/day at 512 tokens avg
[28:52] Jordan Patel: we'll run a cost estimate spreadsheet; rough back-of-envelope for the current sandbox config is $X/day — we'll send a detailed breakdown after the perf run.

[31:00] Daniel Park: also wanted to flag procurement timing — if this goes well procurement needs a 30 day lead to complete PO & review contracts
[31:10] Jordan Patel: understood, we'll align timeline accordingly.

[33:20] Maya Rivera: quick note on instrumentation — use our tracing hooks to capture request_id, batch_id, model_variant, token_count; that helps us diagnose any outliers during the perf run. instrumenting early will speed debugging.

[35:05] Sofia Lopez: ok we'll add those tracing headers to the staging deployment, do you have example headers?
[35:12] Ethan Cho: yes we'll paste an example in the doc; small mismatch in header name occurred before (x-rw-req vs x-redwood-req) so we'll standardize in the runbook.

[37:40] Jordan Patel: sounds good. before we close any other open questions?
[37:50] Marcus Reed: just one: competitors — we ran a small side-by-side vs AWS Bedrock and saw similar latency but Bedrock's pricing model got complicated. curious if Redwood can provide a head-to-head perf/cost sheet.
[38:05] Jordan Patel: yeah we can provide a competitive sheet with normalized tokens/latency metrics. we'll include that in the follow-up package.

[40:00] Dr. Priya Singh: ok no more questions
[40:05] Jordan Patel: great, recap of next steps and owners: Maya - eval spreadsheet and tuned prompt set; Ethan - network diagram & egress IPs; Jordan - pricing for dedicated pilot and SOC2 pack; Sofia - share final creds and confirm VPC peering; Priya - share extended test cases. We'll target the perf benchmark week of 2027-02-22 and a follow-up sync after the run.

[42:30] Marcus Reed: sounds good thanks everyone
[42:35] Jordan Patel: thanks all, we'll send notes and slide deck (short) — links: security pack (to be uploaded), evals (to be uploaded), perf template: https://redwood.app/poc/nexa/perf-template
[43:05] Dr. Priya Singh: thank you
[43:10] Maya Rivera: thanks
[43:12] Ethan Cho: thanks, bye
[43:15] Sofia Lopez: bye

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains occasional name misspellings and product name variations: "Redwood Dedi" / "Redwood Dedicated" / "Redwood Private" spelled inconsistently. References to links are placeholders to represent shared artifacts.
